summary: The Sydney Swans lead AFLW attendance, averaging 4,365 over four home games, less than two years after their first women's match. The club has focused on local communities and enhanced match-day experiences such as gourmet food boxes and local microbreweries. The article also covers wider AFLW crowd trends, the limited Matildas effect, and AFL changes like longer quarters meant to boost scoring.
one_line: The Sydney Swans top AFLW attendances with local, food-focused match days, while league-wide crowds hover around 2,500 and the Matildas boost proves limited.
key_facts: The Sydney Swans average 4,365 fans from four home games, 124 more than the next best AFLW club, Adelaide.
The Swans' final regular-season home match is a pride match against Collingwood at Henson Park on Sunday, with a crowd of over 4,000 expected.
Loretta Johns, executive GM of marketing at the Swans, said the club has targeted local communities and made match days compelling on and off the field.

Nicole Livingstone, AFL general manager of women's football, said the Swans' offering was 'uniquely Sydney', including quince paste, hand-picked grapes, cheddar and biscuits in a wrapped box at North Sydney Oval.
At Henson Park in Sydney's inner west, the Swans invited local microbreweries and promoted through their clientele.
The Swans went winless in 2022, but won their first AFLW match in round one this season and are within a game of the top eight with two rounds to play.
5,474 fans attended North Sydney Oval for the Swans' first AFLW victory this season.
Average AFLW attendance is a little over 2,500 per match this year, roughly on par with previous seasons, and below targets that could speed up extending the season from 10 games to 12 by 2025.
Some clubs recorded crowds under 1,500, in markets such as Melbourne, Perth, Blacktown and the Gold Coast.

The A-League Women opened with a crowd of over 11,000 in Sydney, but later games, including two sub-2,000 crowds in Perth, suggest the Matildas effect has had limited impact on domestic women's sport.
The AFL introduced longer quarters and an interchange cap, adding eight minutes of game time per match on average, and rounds now regularly exceed 100 goals.
The Swans beat the Western Bulldogs 14-12-96 to 6-3-39, and Chloe Molloy set a new AFLW record with 17 score involvements.
Livingstone said only a game separates ladder positions five to 13.
